chapter: Lucky Roberts, Armstrong and the big-band rivalries
title: Depression years and joining Lucky Roberts
summary: As times got rough in 1931-32 Butler joined Lucky Roberts's society orchestra, which demanded classics, the latest numbers and impeccable deportment.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: very, very rough. So it got so rough until even Father Devine, he come into action. He's -- the apples was coming on the scene. It was rough, very, very rough. However, during that time I was very, very lucky. And after that, I think it was $100.00 and something then, but I wouldn't work because the rent was paid for a year.

Seems like something struck and tore my kingdom down. Seems like I was looking for a certain individual and she didn't show for about three months. (Inaudible). Well, the result was I'd been getting -- I started to play with Lucky Roberts, because I've always been interested in singing and I could sing in the quartet. But I was afraid to sing by myself. So Lucky Roberts and they're talking about making money. If Lucky Roberts take you in the band, you got $100.00. But you had to know all these new numbers, you had to know the classics, you had to know everything. And your deportment had to be just that, you could not come in -- you had to be just right. Even your table manners had to be beautiful because, you know, when you play for these (inaudible) and all these people, you're going to sit at the table and you're going to be reaching over there, knocking all that silver platters and everything. And the waiters/served you and going on like that. And Lucky said (inaudible) you wear this. And then when we'd go on the boat, you wear this, and you will get this and (inaudible) because the boat may leave. You'd take it to
Bermuda or take it up and take it up to Pompton Lakes. But there wasn't none of that, 'My dog got out, that's why I'm late.' No, no. He wouldn't have that.
And this man -- you knew it was a genius when he hit the piano.
Well, I played with Lucky a long time. And then with Lucky Millinder
